mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% in a single month leads to a near-term negative S&P 500 20-day forward return due to tightened financing conditions for corporate debt issuance.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% in a month
regime_hint: Rising Fed Funds rate surprise in a restrictive policy phase
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during the same month of the Fed Funds spike (two-tailed t-test, p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in unemployment claims exceeding 200,000 for two consecutive months coincides with a negative S&P 500 60-day forward return as investor sentiment deteriorates on labor market weakness.
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window following the trigger, 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (one-tailed test, p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly coincident rise in both HOUST (consumer confidence) and RSAFS (retail sales) above their 50th percentile for the past 12 months predicts a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return as strong demand signals corporate earnings resilience.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 50th percentile and RSAFS > 50th percentile in the same month
regime_hint: Rebound in consumer and retail demand
failure_condition: No statistically significant positive 20-day forward return (two-tailed test, p > 0.05) during 30 such triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly contraction in INDPRO (industrial production) by more than 2% followed within the same month by a decline in CPIAUCSL (inflation) predicts a negative S&P 500 5-day forward return as weak output and lower price pressures weigh on equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls > -2% in a month and CPIAUCSL falls in the same month
failure_condition: Over 10 such events, the 5-day forward returns are not statistically negative (one-tailed test, p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 4-month decline in UNRATE (unemployment rate) below 4.5% predicts a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return as low labor market friction supports equity risk appetite.
failure_condition: During qualifying UNRATE periods, 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (two-tailed test, p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden one-month drop in GDPC1 (real private consumption) by over 3% followed by a month of rising PAYEMS (employment) predicts a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as a potential bottom in economic cycle.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls > -3% in a month and PAYEMS rises in the following month
regime_hint: Cyclical trough indicated by consumption weakness and labor recovery
failure_condition: No significant positive 60-day forward return during 10 such events (two-tailed test, p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent 6-month decline in CPIAUCSL (CPI) below 3% suggests deflationary pressure, which is associated with a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return as risk premia compress.
failure_condition: During such CPIAUCSL deflation periods, 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than average (two-tailed test, p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A regime shift to rising consumer confidence (HOUST > 110) and simultaneously falling industrial production (INDPRO < 100) predicts a negative S&P 500 20-day forward return as conflicting labor and supply signals create uncertainty.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 110 and INDPRO < 100 in the same month
failure_condition: Over 10 such months, 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative (one-tailed test, p > 0.05).
